title: SLO Governance for Multi‑Tenant Inference
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
=======
This document defines SLO governance, error‑budget policies, and capacity guidance specific to Redwood's multi‑tenant inference services (hosted + dedicated). It codifies how we set per‑model and per‑tenant SLOs, handle error‑budget consumption, and coordinate capacity in the presence of model variants (quantized, fp16), prefix/KV caching, and routing fallbacks. This guidance is intended for SREs, runtime engineers, and product owners who own tenant contracts and model onboarding.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all inference endpoints exposed by the Redwood API (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) that share serving pools in hosted or dedicated modes.
- Does NOT replace enterprise SLA contracts for Dedicated customers but informs mapping between SLOs and contractual SLAs.
- Covers: SLO metric definitions, error budget burn policies, capacity heuristics, alerting and tooling, runbook for sustained burn, and incident review expectations.

Principles
----------
1. Safety-first: preserve availability and routing correctness over micro-optimizations when error budgets are exhausted.
2. Observable metadata: every request must carry tenant_id, model_id, model_variant, and route_tier for accurate attribution.
3. Least surprise for customers: fallback behaviors and preemption policies must be documented per tenant.
4. Cost-aware fairness: capacity preemption must weigh tenant SLA tier and active error budgets.

SLO definitions and examples
---------------------------
We maintain two classes of SLOs: correctness/availability and latency. Each SLO is assigned at model-tenant granularity when practical; otherwise at pooled-service level.

Example SLOs (recommended policy):
- Availability (error rate): 99.9% successful responses (HTTP 2xx) per 30d window for production generation endpoints. Error rate measured as ratio of internal_errors + upstream_timeouts to total requests.
- Latency (short-path): P95 < 250ms for embedding endpoints; P95 < 600ms for chat generation (typical small context).
- Long‑tail latency (sustained generation): P99 < 3s for sequences <= 2048 tokens.
- Correctness guardrail (model regressions): less than 1.0% golden‑prompt failure rate per evaluation suite each release.

SLO attribution rules
- Primary labels used: tenant_id, model_id, model_variant, serving_pool, route_tier.
- When tenant-specific instrumentation is missing, defaults to pooled-service SLO and owner notified.

Error budget policy
-------------------
- Error budget = 100% - SLO. For a 99.9% SLO, the monthly error budget is 0.1% of requests.
- Burn thresholds (30-day rolling):
  - Advisory: consumed > 10% of budget in 24h -> page on-call for awareness, start mitigation checklist.
  - Action: consumed > 50% of budget in 24h -> enable automated throttle or routing adjustments per runbook.
  - Emergency: consumed > 80% of budget in 12h -> conservative preemption of non‑critical tenants and forced rollback to last known-good model variant.
- Consumption drivers: infrastructure failures, model regressions (high internal error), traffic spikes, quantization regressions leading to OOM/latency spikes.

Capacity planning heuristics
--------------------------
- Provisioning units: token‑throughput per GPU hour. Use historical per‑model token/s and average token length to estimate daily capacity.
- Reserve formula (90th percentile demand + 25% buffer) for shared hosted pools. Dedicated customers use 95th percentile + contractual headroom.
- Cache hit modeling: measure prefix/KV caching hit rates per tenant. When hit rate > 60%, effective capacity improves non‑linearly; capture this in forecasts.
- Scheduling: prefer colocating tenants with orthogonal peak times to increase GPU utilization. Document tenant timezones and cadence in onboarding.

Operational tooling and alerts
----------------------------
Required telemetry: request count, success/fail counts, latency histograms, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_variant_ooms, per-tenant queue_length. These feed the SLO observability pipeline.

Core alert rules (examples):
- slo_burn_advisory: PromQL: sum(rate(slo_error_count[1h])) / sum(rate(request_count[1h])) > (0.1 * monthly_budget_rate)
- model_variant_oom_rate: sum(rate(model_variant_oom_total[5m])) by (model_variant) > 0.001 -> page oncall
- cache_degradation: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate[15m]) < 0.45 and traffic_growth_rate > 2x baseline -> create ticket for cache tuning

(See Appendix A for deployable alert YAML samples.)

Runbook: sustained error budget burn (operator workflow)
----------------------------------------------------
1. Triage (0-15min):
   - Confirm burn using SLO dashboard and verify affected tenants and model variants.
   - Determine whether cause is infra (node OOM, kernel crash), runtime (inference kernel regression), or model (behavioral failure).
2. Immediate mitigation (15-60min):
   - If infra: trigger capacity rebalancer to divert traffic to healthy pools and spin ephemeral backfills.
   - If runtime/model: roll back recent runtime or model rollouts using canary rollback endpoints.
   - Apply soft-throttles for low-priority tenants (per preconfigured priority ledger).
3. Stabilize (1-6h):
   - Force route to a higher‑stability variant (fp16 -> int8 fallback only with QA approval unless emergency).
   - Temporarily increase dedicated reserve if contractual and available.
4. Post-stabilization (6-72h):
   - Open incident record and begin incident review process if error budget consumption exceeded emergency threshold.

Incident review expectations
--------------------------
- For any event that triggered the Emergency threshold, an incident review document must be filed within 72 hours. Required sections: timeline, annotated telemetry traces, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and SLO impact table.
- RCA checklist must include: model variant commit IDs, runtime version, exact node ids, capacity shifts, and a sample of failed requests (sanitized for PII).
- Action items should be owner-assigned and tracked in the SRE backlog. Follow-up meeting within 7 days.

Reliability initiatives and experiments
-------------------------------------
The SRE org will run targeted initiatives to reduce long-tail latency and improve multi-tenant fairness. Proposed experiments:
- Adaptive batch sizing per tenant to maintain latency SLOs while maximizing throughput. Success metric: 15% reduced cost per 1k tokens with no P95 regressions.
- Predictive cache prewarm based on model access patterns; measure reduction in cold-start latency.
- Fairshare scheduler pilot that weights tenant backlog by SLO urgency and contract tier. Evaluate on a weekend traffic test.

Ownership and cadence
---------------------
- SLO owner: runtime-sre team (primary), product owner for tenant-level SLO signoff.
- Review cadence: SLOs reviewed quarterly; emergency thresholds and capacity headroom reviewed monthly with product and sales for Dedicated accounts.
- Onboarding: new tenants must pass the "SLO-readiness checklist" (see related page) before moving to production routing.

Appendix A — Example alert rule (deployable YAML snippet described)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The following is an example alert rule to detect sustained P95 latency regressions for a model variant: 

name: model-variant-p95-latency-regression
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant)) > 0.95 *  baseline_p95_seconds
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "P95 latency regression detected for {{ $labels.model_variant }}"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/sustained-error-budget-burn-runbook"

Appendix B — Capacity estimation table (example)
------------------------------------------------
This table is an example used during onboarding (columns are descriptive):
- tenant_id: acme-finance
- model_id: gptx-3.2b-quant
- avg_tokens_per_req: 120
- requests_per_min_peak: 350
- estimated_tokens_per_hour_peak: 120 * 350 * 60 = 2,520,000
- gpus_required_at_peak (rule of thumb): ceil(estimated_tokens_per_hour_peak / 1.2e6) = 3

Notes and exceptions
--------------------
- Dedicated customers with contractual SLAs can request fixed SLO pinning; SRE will create a dedicated SLO document and link it to this governance page.
- Any deviation from the thresholds in this document requires approval from the SRE manager and the product owner.

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-11-05: Created by Maya Chen
- 2027-02-10: Added cache modeling heuristics (reviewers: Priya Sharma)
- 2027-08-12: Expanded runbook to include model‑variant rollback specifics and emergency preemption guidance

Glossary
--------
- serving_pool: a logical pool of GPUs with shared runtime and isolation characteristics.
- route_tier: routing policy label representing priority (gold, silver, bronze).
- model_variant: compiled/quantized build of a model (eg: gptx-3.2b-fp16, -int8-v1).

End of document."
